tex_content.label: R_0cannbhd
tex_content.html:
For $0<\epsilon <1$ there is $r>0$ such that $R(x_0,t_0)\ge r^{-2}$ implies $t_0>r^2$ and a strong $(C(\epsilon ),\epsilon )$-canonical neighborhood at $(x_0,t_0)$. A strong neck there extends backward for rescaled time $1+\epsilon $.
Proof

↗ prop:standard-flow-kappa-noncollapsed ↗ kaplimit ↗ smlmtflow ↗ limitcannbhd \sketch A highest-curvature counterexample sequence has $Q_n\to \infty $. Noncollapsing, positive pinching, and the inductive canonical-neighborhood bound meet the compactness hypotheses; its $\kappa $-solution limit transfers the required neighborhood back, a contradiction.

□

\label{smlmtflow}
Fix canonical-neighborhood constants $(C,\epsilon)$ and non-collapsing
constants $r>0,\kappa>0$. Let $({\mathcal M}_n,G_n,x_n)$ be based
generalized $3$-dimensional Ricci flows, put $t_n={\bf t}(x_n)$ and
$Q_n=R(x_n)$, and let $M_n$ be the $t_n$-slice. Assume:

dependencies.title: limitcannbhd
dependencies.description:
\label{limitcannbhd}

Fix $0<\epsilon\leq\bar\epsilon'$ and the preceding $C(\epsilon)$.
Let $(\mathcal M_n,G_n,x_n)$ be based generalized Ricci flows with
$\mathbf t(x_n)=0$, no time-slice containing an embedded
$\Ar P^2$ with trivial normal bundle, and a smooth based limit
$(M_\infty,g_\infty(t),(x_\infty,0))$, $-\infty<t\leq0$, which is
a $\kappa$-solution. Then $x_n$ has a strong
$(C,\epsilon)$-canonical neighborhood for all sufficiently large
$n$.
\end{corollary}
